title: Open- label study in children and adolescents with migraine: Acute Treatment
official: C4951003 - Phase 3, multicenter, open-label study to assess the long-term safety and tolerability of rimegepant for the acute treatment of migraine (with or without aura) in children and adolescents ≥ 6 to < 18 years of age
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of rimegepant in children and adolescents (age ≥ 6 to < 18 years of age).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. History of migraine (with or without aura) for ≥ 6 months before Screening.
2. History of 1 to 8 moderate or severe attacks per month during the 2 months prior to screening.
3. Participant had 1 or more migraine days requiring treatment during the Observation Phase.
4. Participants on prophylactic migraine medication are permitted to remain on therapy if the dose has been stable for at least 12 weeks prior to the Screening Visit.
5. Participants are required to verbally distinguish between migraine and other types of headaches.
6. Participants must have a body weight > 15 kg. For EU countries only: Participants 12 to < 18 years of age must have a body weight of >25 kg.
7. Participants must have adequate venous access for blood sampling. 8.
8. Participants 6 to < 18 years of age (participants must not reach their 18th birthday on or before enrollment into the study).Baseline visit).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participant has a history of cluster headache or hemiplegic migraine headache. 2.
2. The participant has a confounding and clinically significant pain syndrome that may interfere with their ability to participate in this study.
3. The participant has any current psychiatric condition that is uncontrolled and/or untreated for a minimum of 6 months prior to the Screening Visit. Participants with a lifetime history of psychosis and/or mania are excluded.
4. History of suicidal behavior or the participant is at risk of self-harm or harm to others.
5. History of major psychiatric disorder.
6. The participant has a current diagnosis or history of substance abuse.
7. The participant has reported current use of or has tested positive at the Screening visit for drugs of abuse.
